citation.title: Effects of 10-Day Complete Fasting on Physiological Homeostasis, Nutrition and Health Markers in Male Adults

population.description: Thirteen Chinese men (mean weight 72.1 +/- 11.9 kg) with no history of eating disorders or chronic illness, including diabetes; screened by medical examination, no glucose test reported, hence unselected. Mean +/- SD printed; age and BMI ranges as observed.

protocols.name: bf_strip
protocols.description: Baseline (BF, before fasting) morning capillary strip sample (FreeStyle Optium), sampled 'everyday morning', hour not printed; overnight fast of 10 h assumed (not printed); 30-minute arm read at minutes 29-30, clock hour of the sample taken as 08:00

protocols.name: cf4_strip
protocols.description: Water-only fast (Nongfu Spring water ad libitum, normal ambulatory activity). Day N of the complete fast (CF) is sampled in the morning; the paper does not print the time of the last meal or when CF day 1 began (phases: 3-day BL, 10-day CF, consecutive days; BF1 is the day before fasting), so hours since the last meal are assumed: 10 h (overnight) at the first fasting morning, CF1, plus 24 h per further day, H = 10 + 24*(N-1); this is a lower-end reading and could be about a day longer if the last meal was before the BF1 evening. Fast water-only (Nongfu Spring mineral water ad libitum), normal ambulatory activity within a 'mild-intensity lifestyle program' (no sessions described). CF4 capillary strip sample (everyday morning, hour not printed, 08:00 assumed): H = 10 + 24*3 = 82 h. 30-minute arm read at minutes 29-30

protocols.name: bf_venous
protocols.description: Baseline (BF1, 1 day before fasting) venous blood at 07:00 (stated); overnight fast of 10 h assumed (not printed); 30-minute arm read at minutes 29-30

left_out.what: Glucose and BHB on the other fasting days, including CF1 (glucose 4.18 +/- 0.54 mmol/L; BHB 1.308 +/- 1.053 mmol/L, against 0.177 at BF): the paper does not print when the last meal was taken, and under the only available convention (10 h at the first fasting morning) CF1 would equal the baseline morning although its printed BHB is several-fold higher, so the day-to-hours mapping itself is doubtful
BHB peak: Results say the highest BHB was on CF5 (no value) and the Discussion gives 5.616 +/- 0.911 mmol/L on CF8; the two days disagree
Daily glucose and BHB curves over the 10-day fast and refeeding (Figure 5a)
